source.author: ov
source.text: Funeribus fessi postquam mortalia cernunt temptamenta nihil, nihil artes posse medentum, auxilium caeleste petunt mediamque tenentes orbis humum Delphos adeunt, oracula Phoebi, utque salutifera miseris succurrere rebus sorte velit tantaeque urbis mala finiat, orant: et locus et laurus et, quas habet ipse, pharetras intremuere simul, cortinaque reddidit imo hanc adyto vocem pavefactaque pectora movit:
source.text_original: Funeribus fessi postquam mortalia cernunt / temptamenta nihil, nihil artes posse medentum, / auxilium caeleste petunt mediamque tenentes / orbis humum Delphos adeunt, oracula Phoebi, / utque salutifera miseris succurrere rebus / sorte velit tantaeque urbis mala finiat, orant: / et locus et laurus et, quas habet ipse, pharetras / intremuere simul, cortinaque reddidit imo / hanc adyto vocem pavefactaque pectora movit:
source.text_english: Wearied by funerals, after they see that mortal remedies can accomplish nothing, that nothing can the skills of healers, they seek heavenly aid and, holding the earth at the middle of the world, go to Delphos, the oracles of Phoebus, and pray that by his lot he may choose to bring help to their wretched circumstances and put an end to the evils of so great a city: and the place and the laurel and the quivers that he himself has all trembled together, and the tripod from the depths of the shrine returned this voice, and shook the frightened hearts:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Omnis avet quae iam bellis spectataque fama turba ducum, primae seu quos in flore iuventae temptamenta tenent necdum data copia rerum:
reuse.text_original: Omnis avet quae iam bellis spectataque fama / turba ducum, primae seu quos in flore iuventae / temptamenta tenent necdum data copia rerum: /
reuse.text_english: All the whole crowd of leaders, already famed and tested in wars, whether those whom the first bloom of youth still holds in their first attempts and to whom no full opportunity has yet been given, longs for it.
